missingness_treatment: CORRECTED 2026-09-13, then REVISED again same day -- see transport_missingness.csv and transport_definition.md for the full reconstruction; do not read this cell without those files. A prior pass wrongly treated 2,247 of 4,655 travellers as unanswered/missing; those are 1,997 walkers + 27 cyclists + 223 drivers, identified by the survey's own routing questions, not nonresponse. A second pass wrongly resolved an apparent Q433bPay category-list discrepancy as a PDF-extraction artifact; that resolution is withdrawn -- it is an open, unresolved mismatch between the instrument (which prints only 6 categories for the driver payment-period question) and the exported .dta's value labels (which show 8, including 'per year'/'package trips'), with two live scenarios carried forward rather than one chosen. A third correction rebuilt the hitchhike/listed-mode missingness at the JOURNEY level (all four reported travel legs) rather than the first leg alone: 2,238, not 2,242, first legs carry a usable numeric cost, and 18 people whose first leg was free went on to pay on a later leg of the same journey and were wrongly zeroed out. CORRECTED AGAIN 2026-09-14: two more classifier bugs fixed -- a named payment period with a reported cost of exactly R0 was being counted as a positive cost instead of a legitimate zero (2 hitchhike/listed-mode journeys + 2 drivers affected), and a 'do not know' payment-period leg was not being treated as unresolved when another leg in the same journey was positive (no records currently affected, but now enforced and regression-tested). Current verified breakdown (Scenario A / Scenario B for the disputed driver codes): legitimate zero fares 2,169 (46.6%) / 2,239 (48.1%); usable numeric cost (strictly positive) 2,390 (51.3%) in both scenarios; ambiguous (named period, unspecified cost) 12 (0.3%) in both; genuine nonresponse 84 (1.8%) / 14 (0.3%). UPDATED 2026-09-14: the driver-side per-period reconstruction figures cited in transport_provisional_reconstruction.csv were corrected (a sentinel-handling bug had included the Q434bCost==9999 'Unspecified' sentinel as a literal R9,999 fare in 5 records; corrected per-single-trip/return-trip/weekly driver means are R96.60/R260.31/R353.12, not the previously reported R223.55/R909.56/R920.53). The hitchhike/listed-mode 'usable numeric cost' population (2,256) is now further split into 2,254 fully-costed journeys (every administered leg resolves to a known value) and 2 partially-observed journeys (a confirmed positive leg alongside another unresolved leg) -- these totals were not separated before. Both files now regenerate reproducibly from scripts/build_transport_review_tables.py rather than uncommitted scratch scripts. 2026-09-14: driver positive-only and numeric-zero-inclusive means are now reported as separately labelled rows in transport_provisional_reconstruction.csv, rather than only the positive-only figure.
units: ratio of a day-conditional transport cost to one day's wage (dimensionless)
estimator: ratio of two independently-weighted point estimates
uncertainty_method: Nonparametric bootstrap (2,000 resamples), cost and wage populations resampled independently each draw. No cluster/PSU adjustment attempted or its absence checked for NHTS specifically.
model_counterpart: src/moments.py transport_budget_share() -- total transport spend over total effective search trips in a window, divided by the daily wage
open_audit_findings: The payment-period conversion (single trip vs return trip vs week/month/year, separately for the listed-mode/hitchhike group and the driver block), and the Scenario A/B choice for the disputed Q433bPay codes 5-6, are the concrete remaining P2.3 tasks -- see transport_definition.md for the exact open decisions and for review-only unconverted per-period cost figures (transport_provisional_reconstruction.csv). No corrected transport_budget_share is reported until that reconstruction is complete and verified, per instruction. No design-effect/clustering check has been run for NHTS specifically. The claim that per-single-trip costs need no conversion 'under any excursion definition' was corrected 2026-09-14: it holds only once the excursion is defined as one-direction, not unconditionally -- see transport_definition.md. 2026-09-14: decision-ready candidate journey-level transport estimates, now with a corrected frequency-conversion bug (weekly/monthly fares previously ignored the excursion definition), person weighting as the primary approach (unweighted as diagnostic), round-trip proposed as the primary excursion unit (matches the model's own return-fare interpretation -- see src/calibrate.py), and a candidate transport-to-wage ratio of ~0.197-0.199 (95% bootstrap CI, driver-scenario sensitivity), roughly double the current 0.1058 -- see transport_candidate_estimates.md/.csv and transport_wage_ratio_candidates.csv. Still review output only; no single estimate adopted, and this is a proposal for review, not a decision.

Working-age is not itself defined to an exact age range in the extracted text (StatsSA's conventional 15-64 assumed, not independently confirmed).
labour_market_universe: CONFIRMED population-based, not labour-force-based: the paper's own text and Table 5b's title ('Spatial Correlates of Share of the Adult Population Employed') both describe the dependent variable as the share of the working-age POPULATION employed -- denominator is everyone working-age, not the labour force.

weights: sub-place-level population weights (paper's own specification); not applicable to this project beyond citing the paper's coefficient
missingness_treatment: not applicable (published coefficient, no microdata used by this project)
units: percentage points of employment share per 10 percentile points of within-city travel-time rank
estimator: OLS regression coefficient (paper's own specification; no population-density control per the notebook's own header note; robustness checked against a spatial-error specification with population density, per the paper's Table 5a/5b pairing)
uncertainty_method: Paper's own reported t-statistics; reconstructed per-city sampling SE = |coefficient|/|t-statistic| (Johannesburg 1.10, Cape Town 0.84, eThekwini 0.66), kept separate from moments.csv's standard_error, which is instead the cross-city sample SD (1.4048) used as a calibration-uncertainty scale, not a sampling SE
model_counterpart: src/moments.py distance_gradient_slope() -- OLS slope of EMPLOYED (share of the model's own agent/labour-force population) on percentile rank of distance_to_cbd
open_audit_findings: DECIDED 2026-09-13: removed from the fitted MSM target set (option 1 of three presented). Retained only as a QUALITATIVE external benchmark -- not described as independent quantitative validation, since it is not disjoint data collected for that purpose and the confirmed population/labour-force mismatch (verified against Literature/baez_full.txt, not just the table title: the paper's dependent variable is the working-age POPULATION employment share; the model's distance_gradient_slope() is necessarily labour-force-based) means even a directional check carries an unknown, unsigned compositional bias term. E/Pop = (E/LF)*(LF/Pop), so the paper's slope conflates the model's own estimand with however labour-force participation varies with distance -- a channel the paper does not report and no participation-by-distance profile exists to correct for. The retained (discouraged_share, transport_budget_share, long_term_share) set is now exactly identified against the 3 remaining estimated parameters -- see the bounded pre-calibration specification for the reassessed identification result.
